stories.title: Kyiv's new reality: Russian drones by night — and now by day
stories.summary: More than a week of strikes by jet-powered Russian drones has disrupted schools, work and transport … and left Ukraine, which lacks air defense supplies, feeling vulnerable.

stories.title: Trump's arch may break ground without final approval. Veterans are trying to stop it
stories.summary: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum says "excavation work" will begin in the next two weeks, without approval from a key federal body. Veterans who sued over the arch want a judge to intervene before then.

stories.title: Dolly Parton's music rises on the charts
stories.summary: The late country singer's hits are making a mark on the pop charts following her death. Many are charting higher than they ever have before — and the rise of country music might play a role.

stories.title: Nepal flood waters have receded, but threats to physical and mental health are growing
stories.summary: Seven hospitals/health centers have been damaged in the floods, some completely wiped out. Medical workers are concerned about interrupted routine care, risk of waterborne and communicable disease outbreaks in "holding centers" and the mental health impacts of the disaster.

stories.title: El-Sayed divided Michigan Democrats. Whether they unify could decide Senate control
stories.summary: After a bruising primary, Democrats in Michigan are working to unify their coalition ahead of what is expected to be a razor-thin Senate race this fall for a seat they need to hold if they hope to retake the Senate majority.

stories.title: Who owns the beach? A heated battle plays out in the Florida Panhandle
stories.summary: After years of fighting over who gets to use the beach, and where, in Walton County, Florida, public-use advocates are calling for a state constitutional amendment to finally settle the matter.
